messages:
Maria (CS): FYI: Acme reported repeated duplicate chunks after reconnecting their SSE stream. They see partial output, then on reconnect the model replays same tokens plus continues, resulting in duplicated text and extra billing. Logs attached by customer.
Maria (CS): customer says this happens when network blips for ~2-4s. They retry immediately and get duplicates. They pasted a short capture: \n``` 
<open SSE connection>
event: partial\ndata: {\"text\":\"Hello, wor\"}\n<TCP drop>\n<reconnect with same idempotency-key>\nevent: partial\ndata: {\"text\":\"Hello, world\"}\n```
Maria (CS): they claim idempotency-key is set client-side but they didn't supply a resume token. They expected server to resume from last event-id instead of re-generating.
Ingrid (SRE): thanks — can you paste the exact request headers + timestamps? also which client lib/version? SSE reconnection semantics vary.
Maria (CS): sent headers: `Idempotency-Key: acme-req-4721`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Connection: keep-alive` and `User-Agent: acme-sdks/1.2.3`. timestamps: first open 2026-05-17T14:01:12Z, reconnect 14:01:15Z, second disconnect 14:01:18Z.
Lucas (Support): quick note: customer is worried about billing duplicate tokens. Is there a policy we can point to re: resumed/incomplete streams? :thinking_face:
Kai (Eng Runtime): short answer: our current model treats each accepted generation as billable. If a reconnect causes a fresh generation to be accepted (no resume semantics used), it will count. We do have a short dedupe window for identical generation hashes when `Idempotency-Key` matches, but only for non-streaming endpoints. Streaming resume is still a gap.
Kai (Eng Runtime): some ideas:
- server-side resume support using `Last-Event-ID`/`Resume-Token` so clients can request continuation instead of restart
- when resume not requested, apply server dedupe: keep a per-idempotency recent generation cache (TTL ~60s) and suppress duplicate events if generation hash matches
- better client guidance: exponential backoff + jitter before immediate reconnect to avoid repeated replays
Ingrid (SRE): re reproduce steps I'd like: 1) open SSE; 2) let it stream partial chunk (simulate network drop) after N tokens; 3) reconnect immediately with same idempotency-key; 4) observe duplication. We should run across multiple model sizes.
Maria (CS): customer shared a cURL repro. posting below, maybe helpful for eng: \n```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Idempotency-Key: acme-req-4721" \
     -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","prompt":"Hello","stream":true}' \
     "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
# drop TCP after partial then re-run same command immediately
```
Kai (Eng Runtime): nice. For a short-term mitigation I suggest telling the customer to: 1) include a `Resume-Token` header returned by the server on first partial event (we can add a quick patch) OR 2) use an exponential backoff on reconnects (start 150ms, *2 up to 5s + random jitter) and treat identical events as idempotent client-side.
Kai (Eng Runtime): server-side dedupe sketch:\n```
# pseudocode
cache_key = sha256(idempotency_key + model + prompt_hash)
if cache.exists(cache_key) and cache[cache_key].generation_hash == new_generation_hash:
  drop or annotate repeated events as dup
else:
  accept & store cache[cache_key] = {generation_hash, timestamp}
```
Ingrid (SRE): couple of notes — dup suppression must not silently drop user-visible tokens; better to mark as duplicate and send `event: dup-suppressed` with `data: {reason: "resumed-duplicate", original_ts: 1769001234}` so clients can reconcile.
Lucas (Support): Can we make a short customer-facing workaround doc? One-liner: "If you see duplicates after reconnect, use resume-token + exponential backoff; if unavailable, dedupe on client using `generation_id` and drop repeated prefixes."
Maria (CS): customer asked whether we can retroactively credit duplicate charges. They're small but want reassurance. Any billing folks around? tagging billing later.
Kai (Eng Runtime): technical feasibility: implement short-term server dedupe for streaming endpoints (60s TTL) + add `Resume-Token` header in partial events within next sprint. Need 1 engineer ~3-4 days for safe rollout + tests.
Ingrid (SRE): I'll add an automated integration test that simulates flaky network and immediate reconnect with same idempotency key to validate no duplicated final outputs. Also add telemetry to count resumed-duplicates.
support-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-3381 streaming-reconnect-duplicates. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-3381
Maria (CS): OK assigning: Kai -> implement dedupe + resume-token, Ingrid -> tests + telemetry, Lucas -> customer workaround doc and response. I'll ping customer with temporary mitigation and ask them to enable jitter/backoff.
Kai (Eng Runtime): small RFC note for implementation: prefer using `Last-Event-ID` (standard SSE) and also include a `X-Resume-Token` with opaque resume pointer if we can't rely on event-id semantics for partial chunks.
Maria (CS): thanks team. I'll update thread with customer follow-up and paste customer's logs once they send the full trace. :thumbsup:
